name: Apollo 8
first: First humans to leave low Earth orbit + orbit the Moon
dispatch: Apollo 8 was a bet placed in a hurry. Intelligence suggested the Soviets might loop a crew around the Moon first, so in the summer of 1968 NASA tore up the flight plan and sent three men to lunar orbit on only the third launch of a rocket that had never carried a crew. It should have been reckless. Instead it became the year's one piece of good news — 1968 had been assassinations, Vietnam, cities on fire — and on Christmas Eve a billion people heard Genesis read from lunar orbit and, in Bill Anders' photograph, watched their whole world rise over a dead horizon for the first time. Apollo 11 is remembered for the Moon. Apollo 8 is the one that showed us the Earth.
description: The first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, the first to escape Earth gravity, and the first to orbit the Moon. Launched 1968-12-21 on the first crewed flight of the Saturn V (AS-503), Apollo 8 entered lunar orbit on Christmas Eve 1968. Anders' "Earthrise" photograph during the fourth orbit became one of the most influential images in history. The crew read from Genesis on live television to ~1 billion viewers — the largest TV audience to that date. 10 orbits later they fired the SPS engine for TEI on the far side of the Moon, returning to Pacific splashdown 1968-12-27. NASA had decided in August 1968 to swap Apollo 8's payload from a high-Earth-orbit LM test to a lunar-orbit CSM-only mission after CIA intelligence suggested the USSR might attempt a circumlunar flight first.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Saturn V (AS-503) from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A 1968-12-21 12:51 UTC — first crewed Saturn V flight.

events.label: TLI
events.note: Trans-lunar injection burn — first crewed escape of Earth gravity. S-IVB ∆v ~3.05 km/s.

events.label: LOI
events.note: Lunar orbit insertion behind the Moon, out of radio contact. SPS burn ~0.91 km/s. First humans to orbit another body.

events.label: EARTHRISE
events.note: Anders photographs Earth rising over the lunar horizon during the fourth orbit (1968-12-24, AS08-14-2383).

events.label: GENESIS READING
events.note: Crew reads from Genesis on live TV to ~1 billion viewers — largest live TV audience to that date.

events.label: TEI
events.note: Trans-Earth injection behind the Moon (1968-12-25 06:10 UTC). SPS ∆v ~1.07 km/s.

events.label: SPLASHDOWN
events.note: CM splashed down in North Pacific 1968-12-27. Recovery by USS Yorktown.
